ruling.recommended_action: Send to a human reviewer for the untied named-road consent; reviewer to obtain the driven-path road data (or the driver's GPS trace) and, if the 09:53–10:01 segment is shown not to be Bedok North Avenue 3, issue a refund_partial of 2.15 km × $1.4099/km = $3.03 plus a driver account review (RD-6, F17). Do not execute any refund automatically.
ruling.reasoning:
The trip is a metered RydeTAXI service: the fare breakdown charges distance $31.47 for 22.32 km and time at the meter, so extra kilometres pass straight into what the rider pays [F7][RD-2]. Only one off-route segment exists — 09:53–10:01, 4.49 km driven where the optimal route covers 2.33 km, adding 2.15 km [F3][RD-1]. The trace settles the traffic screen against the driver: no qualifying LTA incident appears on the replaced stretch, and a speed band alone does not exempt, so RD-4 gives no ground [F12][F14][RD-4]. A band-2 record on the PIE over 09:27–09:53 [F12] is corroborative only and, under RD-4(b)/(c), cannot carry the segment by itself, so this is not a "reasonable cause" exemption [RD-4].

Consent exists and is timely: the driver proposed a specific road at 09:50 [F8] and the rider personally answered "可以，走 Bedok North Avenue 3 吧" at 09:50 [F9], before the segment start at 09:53, and the chat record is complete and fully timestamped [F10][F3]. That makes the agreement a SPECIFIC named-road authorisation, not a general "whichever way is faster" route choice [RD-5]. The driver's post-trip statement that the rider agreed [F11] adds nothing, since under RD-5 an agreement appearing only in the driver's own statement is not consent, but it is not needed here [RD-5].

The scope question is therefore the whole case. A specific named-road agreement covers driving on Bedok North Avenue 3 only, and the record must tie the segment to that road [RD-5]. Nothing does: the chat is just the two 09:50 messages with no pin or position [F8][F9][F10], and the GPS fact describes the segment only by distance, deviation and time window, naming no road [F3]. But nothing places the car elsewhere either — no stop away from the agreed road, no driver statement naming a different road, no road name for the driven path — so the record does not settle whether the agreed road is the road driven [F3][F9][RD-5]. Both advocates' stipulated ground is named_road_untied, and the trace leaves the RD-5 scope as the question for me, so the finding on F3 is undetermined, not exempt and not counts [RD-5].

Because the RD-5 finding controls the amount — exempt yields no_action, counts yields a refund of Σ extra_km × this trip's rate — an undetermined segment must go to a person rather than be resolved by presumption, and the record needed to settle it is missing [RD-2][RD-5]. The rate, if a reviewer finds the segment unexempted, is this trip's distance fare ÷ distance km: $31.47 ÷ 22.32 km = $1.4099/km [F7][F4], and 2.15 km × $1.4099/km = $3.03; the remaining $0.49 of the billed excess (2.50 km − 2.15 km) lies outside any segment and is not refundable [F1][F3][F4][RD-2]. I therefore state no amount and escalate.

A refund only follows an adverse finding, and on that branch the driver's profile would matter: 2 route disputes, 2 upheld, in the last 90 days [F17], which on this case becoming a repeated breach triggers the account review under RD-6. Profile facts may not decide the case itself, so this affects only the accompanying account action, and only if the reviewer finds the segment unexempted; I do not set the flag now. The rider's clean record [F16] and the driver's long tenure and 4.72 rating [F17] carry no weight either way on the routing question.
